Note: Draft policy registry: the guide (POLICY-GUIDE.md) in a form tools/check_policy.py checks. Not an EM schema. A policy type is a use case owned by the daemons that consume it; each daemon subscribes to the types it needs. An entry of vrnvl-hmc-platform-policy.json is {Name: <label equal to Type>, Type: <UseCase>Policy, <Section>: {...}, ...} with one section per device kind; several entries (different types) for one target land on one D-Bus object, each type as its own interface xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.<Type>. A type holds flat properties, or one level of nested sub-policy objects (each its own interface <Type>.<SubPolicy>). Targets: a device kind from the topology, a board sensor type, a board name, or the platform.

NsmDeviceCapabilityPolicy.Default: every capability the entity describes is enabled

Variants.Note: absent means every capability the entity describes is enabled; a section lists only what the platform disables
an empty list is not published by EM; the interface existing is the declaration

EndpointPollingPolicy.Note: the poll interval is a setting of the bus, so the sections are transports; the USB recovery threshold differs between USB devices of one platform (CPU 5, GPU SMA none) and stays in the entity file

Naming.Rule: One entry per use case: {Name: <label equal to Type>, Type: <UseCase>Policy}. The device scope is in the structure: one nested section per device kind inside the entry (Gpu, GpuSma, HpmSma, Cpu, BmcRot, BmcErot), or per bus for a bus-level use case (Usb, I2c, Xrot), published by EM as the interface <Type>.<Section>. A property directly on the entry (not in a section) applies to the platform. Nothing is selected by the Name.
